EVERY FIGURE OF THE RUN IS A PLACEHOLDER the generator fills from the record (doc/facts.py) and every sentence whose truth depends on the run is a conditional `[[flag ? when true | when false]]`. The literal numbers are constants of SPEC-pattern-search.md, of the manifest (the genetic codes the genomes carry, the quotas, the lengths) and of the service, each listed under `_assumes` with its source. Every claim follows SPEC-pattern-search.md sections 12.2 and 20, areas.py gen_X, checks.py and service_by_design.json as of 14245fb49. No timing sentence names a cause the run does not isolate.

coverage_gap: *What remains unsupported.* The genetic codes without a positive: the host serves tables 1 to 6, 9 to 16 and 21 to 33, but the genomes of I.2 use 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 11 and 12 alone, so nothing here tests the codon tables of the others; the context stops of tables 27, 28 and 31 (TGA as W, TAA and TAG as Q or E) are not searched as residues, only the stop `*` is, and a stop positive exists for tables 1, 2, 4, 11 and 12 only (the records hold no single-exon protein of tables 3, 5 and 6 whose last 9 residues and stop read in its table). No decapeptide or 20-residue window of table 12 and one of the five table-4 decapeptides hold a codon the table reassigns, so those are tested on the table's sense codons alone (the manifest's skipped list states the three entries: table 4's one 10-residue window, table 12's five 10-residue and three 20-residue windows), and X-table1 reaches tables 3, 4 and 6 only. Peptides longer than k are tested as supported paths with a predicate alone, never as `paths` nor with `labels: all`; substitutions in a peptide are chapter M's. The junction claim is index-empirical: observed on this index, named in the truth, not derived from the records. Via MCP the anchors-only answer of an 11-residue peptide and the slot of a residue outside the alphabet are not shown (the service refuses both at submit, appendix B).

intro: A `protein` pattern is a peptide over the 20 amino acids, the ambiguity codes X (any residue but a stop), B (D or N), Z (E or Q) and J (I or L), and the stop `*` (SPEC-pattern-search section 12.2), read in the NCBI translation table `genetic_code` names (1 to 6, 9 to 16 and 21 to 33; 1, the standard code, is the default; another integer is 400 `genetic_code_unknown`). Its instances are exactly the codon strings of its residues in that table, found by a codon automaton (no superset: a residue's codons are its own, never a per-position union); a stop codon matches `*` and nothing else. A peptide of m residues is a pattern of L = 3m bases: at most 10 residues lie within one k-mer and are searched as chapter P's patterns (the contexts, offsets and `length` in bases), longer peptides are patterns longer than k (chapter L: anchors, paths, supported paths through the automaton). `strands` `reverse` searches the reverse-complemented automaton; the bits of a peptide are exact, residue by residue, and the floor gates them as it gates DNA. Tables 27, 28 and 31 have no unconditional stop codon: `*` admits no codon there, and a peptide holding it is answered `exact` 0 without a search, the note `no_stop_codon`, `stop` null, `work.steps` 0 and `determinism` `full`, wherever it sits in a request (section 12.2). A character outside the alphabet (U, O, a digit) is a `bad_alphabet` slot, the other patterns answered.

Ground truth: the protein validation set of I.2, proteins of the records' genomes with their coding windows of 10, 20 and 30 residues (and the same windows shifted by one or more residues, named with `~`), each window's coding DNA checked against the record's bases on the protein's strand before it is used (a window the record does not hold is never used). The genomes carry the genetic codes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 11 and 12; for a code other than 1 and 11 the builder prefers windows whose coding DNA reads differently in table 1 (a window holding no codon the table reassigns proves nothing about the table), and the manifest's skipped list states where none exists. The property of a decapeptide is chapter P's: every record context of the coding DNA listed on the protein's strand (`contains_source_context`, strand `+` or `-`, the k - L + 1 contexts being 2 for 30 bases); of a longer peptide chapter L's: a supported path verified by the record's taxid at the window's coordinates (`path_record_verified`). Every request names `genetic_code`, `mode`, `max_contexts` 10,000 and `time_budget_ms` 60,000 as in chapter P; the long peptides name `long_search: supported_paths`, `max_paths` 1,024 and a predicate `any` of the taxid with `predicate_only`. Via MCP (`pattern_search`) a `genetic_code` the host does not serve is refused at submit under the service's code, a residue outside the host's `protein_residues` refuses the whole submit (the host refuses the slot), and a peptide of more than 10 residues without `long_search` is refused (the anchors-only answer is not expressible); a peptide is passed through otherwise, `*` included. Each by-design cell names its case; appendix B gives the service's code and text.

X-peptide10.title: decapeptides
X-peptide10.prose: Decapeptides of the validation set searched under their genetic code, balanced per code (table 1: 8 windows; tables 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6: 5 each; table 11: 8; table 12: 5), taken round-robin over the code's genomes, shifted windows included; for tables 2, 3, 5 and 6 every window chosen reads differently in table 1 and for table 4 four of the five do (the titles say so), so a hit there is evidence for the table's reassigned codons and not for the standard code, while table 12's windows and the fifth table-4 window hold no codon the table reassigns and test its sense codons only (the manifest's skipped list states both). The property: every record context of the coding DNA, 2 for 30 bases, is listed on the protein's strand (`contains_source_context`). The rows group the tests by table. [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted} test{n_footnoted:s} did not pass on every arm: {footnoted_text}; the detail block{n_footnoted:s} follow{n_footnoted:v} the table. | In this run every test passed on every arm.]]
X-peptide10.claim: a decapeptide finds its coding DNA under its genetic code

X-peptide-long.title: long peptides
X-peptide-long.prose: Peptides of 20 residues, balanced per code (tables 1 and 11: 4 each; the other six codes: 3 each), and two of 30 residues (tables 1 and 11), searched as supported paths with a predicate `any` of the taxid and `predicate_only`: the record's coding DNA is a supported path selected by the taxid and verified by one of its records at the window's coordinates on the protein's strand (`path_record_verified`). On this index most walks spelling a long peptide are mosaics (section 20.1's measurement), which is why the supported-path search, not the enumeration of every walk, is the route for long peptides; section 20.7 states its cost as the rows the search reads, and the tests are timing class slow. The rows group the tests by table, the 30-residue pair apart.
X-peptide-long.claim: a long peptide's coding DNA is a supported path selected by its taxid and verified by its record

X-table1.title: the wrong code
X-table1.prose: Six decapeptides of genomes with a non-standard code whose coding DNA reads differently in table 1 (ser, table 4; scem, table 3, three windows; tth, table 6, two), searched in table 1: the record's codons are out of reach of the standard code's automaton, so the source contexts are absent from the complete list (`source_absent`), an expected miss that shows the code was applied. The six are the first proteins of the set with such a window; tables 2 and 5 have such windows too (X-peptide10 searches them under their own code) and were not reached, and table 12 has none (the manifest's skipped list).
X-table1.claim: a decapeptide read in the wrong code misses its record

X-stop.title: stop codons
X-stop.prose: X-stop-found: the last 9 residues of a single-exon protein and its stop `*`, read in the protein's table, the 30 bases ending at the stop codon taken from the record: found at the stop codon, every record context on the protein's strand. One per code with stop codons that the genomes carry and a fetched single-exon protein, two for table 11: tables 1 (sce), 2 (hsam), 4 (mge), 11 (eco, twice) and 12 (cal); the codes without such a protein in the records are stated in the manifest's skipped list. X-stop-none: the peptide MKV*LLAAGR in tables 27, 28 and 31, which have no unconditional stop codon: `exact` 0 without a search (`absent`), the note `no_stop_codon`, `stop` null, `work.steps` 0 and `determinism` `full` (section 12.2), an answer that needs no budget and no clock.
X-stop.claim: a stop matches the stop codon of its table and matches nothing where the table has none

X-junction.title: exon junctions
X-junction.prose: A 20-residue window across one exon junction of a spliced protein (one of S. cerevisiae, three of S. pombe), searched as paths in `partial` with `max_paths` 1,024: no path spells the spliced coding DNA (`path_absent`), the record holding the exons apart; the complete list is required (a withheld or cut list reads inconclusive, a stated hiding that cannot have happened fails). The claim is index-empirical ([[manifest_version = 5 ? the manifest tags it so and names the index in the truth | v5 tags it so and names the index in the truth; v4 states it in this prose alone]]): another record of the index, an intronless copy or a cDNA, or a recombination of the graph could spell it, so the absence was observed on this index, not derived from the records, and a failure on another index asks for a re-validation before it reads as a regression.
X-junction.claim: the spliced coding DNA across an exon junction is spelled by no path of this index

X-edge.title: edge inputs
X-edge.prose: Two units. X-edge-ambiguity: a table-11 decapeptide with B in place of its N, Z for its Q, J for its L and X for a residue in its middle (positions 3 to 6): still found, every record context listed (B, Z and J admit the codons of their two residues, X every sense codon). X-edge-other: `genetic_code` 7, which is no table, refused with the exact text naming the tables served (`genetic_code_unknown`); 11 residues (33 bases, longer than k) without `long_search`: answered by its anchors only, `withheld` `paths_later_increment`, `length` 33, `residues` 11, `scope` `long`; and selenocysteine U at position 4 of a decapeptide: a `bad_alphabet` slot with the exact message, the other decapeptide of the request answered. Via MCP the three are decided by the service at submit (the unknown code refused under its own code, the long peptide refused for want of `long_search`, the residue refusing the whole submit): by design, appendix B.
X-edge.claim: ambiguity codes stand for their residues; a wrong code, a long peptide without the opt-in and a residue outside the alphabet are answered as section 12.2 states

X-peptide10.property: A decapeptide of a protein searched under its genetic code finds the coding DNA: every record context listed on the protein's strand.
X-peptide10.note: The rows group the tests by genetic code; for tables 2, 3, 5 and 6 every window reads differently in table 1 and for table 4 four of five, so those rows test the table's reassigned codons; table 12's windows and one of table 4's test the sense codons only.

units.X-peptide-long: A 20- or 30-residue peptide searched as supported paths with a predicate on its taxid: the coding DNA is a selected supported path, record-verified at the window's coordinates on the protein's strand.
units.X-table1: A decapeptide of another code read in table 1: the record's codons are out of reach, the source contexts absent from the complete list (an expected miss).
units.X-stop-found: A protein's last 9 residues and its stop, read in the protein's table: found at the stop codon, every record context on the protein's strand.
units.X-stop-none: A stop in a table without an unconditional stop codon (27, 28, 31): exact 0 without a search, the note no_stop_codon, stop null, work.steps 0, determinism full.
units.X-junction: A 20-residue window across an exon junction, searched as paths: no path spells the spliced DNA in the complete list (index-empirical).
units.X-edge-ambiguity: The ambiguity codes B, Z, J and X stand for their residues: the decapeptide is still found, every record context listed.
units.X-edge-other: An unknown genetic code is refused with the exact text; 11 residues without long_search answer anchors only (withheld paths_later_increment, length 33, residues 11, scope long); U is a bad_alphabet slot beside an answered pattern.
